summary: Iteration 6 backend revalidation of partial-index fix for transactions.client_id. Re-ran /app/backend/tests/test_iteration5_fixes.py (all 13 tests PASS including previously failing test_5_omit_client_id_creates_new_each_time). Added /app/backend/tests/test_iteration6_index_and_mix.py to verify DB-level index shape, explicit repro (two POSTs with no client_id → distinct txn ids AND distinct receipt_numbers), mixing (with client_id then without → distinct), and idempotency regressions (same cid → same txn; different cids → distinct). All 5 new tests PASS. Direct pymongo inspection confirms the transactions collection has 'client_id_unique_partial' (unique=true, partialFilterExpression={'client_id': {'$type': 'string'}}) and NO 'client_id_1' sparse index. Fix confirmed working.
critical_code_review_comments: Partial index migration is idempotent (drops legacy sparse index if present, then creates the new partial one). Good.
Consider adding a lightweight startup log line confirming which of the two branches ran (drop-legacy vs already-migrated) for operational visibility.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 5 index bug (sparse blocking legacy null path) is fully resolved via partial index. Both suites (test_iteration5_fixes.py, test_iteration6_index_and_mix.py) are green as of iter 6. Frontend was already 100% in iter 5 and was intentionally skipped this iteration.
rca of the issue: Original bug: MongoDB sparse-unique index only excludes documents where the indexed field is ABSENT, but Pydantic serialises Optional[str]=None to JSON null which Mongo stores as a present-but-null value → the second insert with client_id=null hit a duplicate-key error on the legacy sparse index. Fix (verified): replace with a partial index whose filter is {client_id: {$type: 'string'}} so null/absent both bypass the unique constraint, while string values remain uniquely enforced. Verified idempotency retained for real client_ids, and null-path now creates distinct txns.
